summary: Strong preliminary report on your Great Barrier Reef monitoring mission. You scoped a clear goal with quantified objectives, justified users and benefits, completed credible 600 km SSO and swath analysis, and presented an exemplary Gantt and contingency plan. You are well placed for the full mission design.
next_steps: Close your weekly coverage gap by testing neighbouring SSO altitudes or wider swath options in STK and quantify revisit time.
Carry your Table 1 contingency triggers forward and keep Table 2 sources linked to each design decision in the final report.
Extend Table 3 hand calculations into fully verified STK coverage plots over the 2,300 km reef length for the final mission.

criteria.C1: You described a clear reef-colour goal with 4 quantified objectives including imaging the 2,300 km reef, and linked AIMS, GBRMPA, CSIRO and BoM needs to objectives with references [1]-[6]. To hold Accomplished, keep requirements traceable to users in final design.
criteria.C2: Your Figure 1 Gantt for weeks 2-10 with completed/planned colours and deadlines, dependency ordering, Table 1 triggers/responses including Week 10 float, and Table 2 sources with STK justification is exemplary. To hold Accomplished, follow that sequence through.
criteria.C3: You showed good progress with STK tutorials 1-4, hand calculations for 600 km SSO with a=6978 km, T=5801 s, 97.8 deg, and interpretation that 60 km swath needs 5 passes for 250 km width. To hold Accomplished, convert this into closed coverage results.
criteria.C4: Your report is logical and easy to read with consistent captions for Figure 1 and Table 3, readable Gantt, and in-text references matched to the list. To hold Accomplished, maintain this structure, labelling and referencing discipline in the final report.
